technical: A phone closes a waiting invite within seconds of you leaving the app. Only DuckDuckGo and Safari have been seen to hold one for about ten.
Chrome on Android reports no IPv6 where Firefox and DuckDuckGo on the same phone and the same Wi-Fi report one. A verdict describes this browser, not the network.
On mobile data, carrier NAT usually blocks a direct connection to anyone outside that network.
A VPN moves both ends somewhere else, which can fix a blocked network or break a working one.

clause.noServer: We run no server, and no copy of your playlists exists anywhere we control.
clause.gateway: The app itself is delivered through a public IPFS gateway, which sees that you loaded it. Your own Kubo node, or the IPFS Companion extension, fetches it from the network instead.
clause.relay: Relay nodes introduce devices to each other and may keep a copy of a playlist so another device can collect it later.
clause.playlist: A playlist you create decides who may write to it - you, and any friend whose identity you let in. It does not decide who may read it: anyone who has its address can.
clause.readingIsOpen: Nothing here is encrypted. A playlist holds links, titles, teachers and tags - put nothing in it you would not put on a shared pinboard.
clause.oembed: When you paste a YouTube or Vimeo link, this browser asks youtube.com or vimeo.com for the title, the thumbnail and, at Vimeo, the length. YouTube tells the length only through its player, so for a YouTube link the player is loaded from youtube-nocookie.com as well, out of sight and without playing; the player fetches its own parts from other Google servers. Apart from that, those services learn nothing from this app before you press play.
clause.embeds: Playing a clip loads it from youtube-nocookie.com, player.vimeo.com or instagram.com, with everything that implies about those services seeing you watch. Apart from the lookup when you paste a link, nothing loads before you click. An Instagram clip is shown through Instagram's own embed page in a frame; none of its scripts run in this app's page.
clause.storage: Your playlists and clips are kept in this browser (IndexedDB) so they are there offline and after a reload. Which clips you marked done, and when, stays on this device only.
clause.identityPasskey: Your passkey identifies you to the other devices. Nobody else can write as you.
clause.identityAnonymous: You are using a random identity that exists only in this browser. Clear its storage and it is gone - along with the right to write to your playlists.
clause.cookies: No tracking cookies are used. Besides your data, the only things saved on this device are your language, theme, and the choice to hide this notice.

consent.identityCreatePrompts: The passkey is asked four times on the way: to be created, to note its identity, for the signing key, and to confirm that key. Before each further prompt the app says what it is for.
consent.identityExistingPrompts: One prompt; on a new device up to three. Before each further prompt the app says what it is for.

create.title: Now the new passkey
create.why: Your device creates the passkey and asks you to confirm it.

store.title: Now the passkey notes which identity is its own
store.why: The passkey keeps a note of the identity that belongs to it. That is how Yoga Clips finds it again when this browser loses its data or you pick up another device. Not every passkey can do this; the note then stays in this browser only.

find.title: Now the passkey says which identity is its own
find.why: The passkey hands out the note it keeps of its identity.

key.title: Now the key your clips are signed with
key.why: Your passkey gives Yoga Clips a secret. From it comes the key that signs your clips - the same key on every device you use this passkey on.

proof.title: Now the confirmation that this key is yours
proof.why: Your passkey confirms once that the signing key belongs to it. Other devices check that before they accept your clips. This browser keeps the confirmation and does not ask for it again.

passkeySteps.notALoop: Each prompt has a purpose of its own; it is not a repeat. With a security key: touch it and, if asked, enter its PIN.
passkeySteps.cancelled: Cancelled before the passkey was asked. You can start again whenever you like.
passkeySteps.cancelledCreated: Cancelled. Your new passkey already exists - "Use an existing passkey" carries on from there.
